chunks: And Faḍālah narrated from Abān, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about two partners, one of whom testified for the other. He said: “His testimony is valid except regarding something in which he has a share.”

key_terms.شَرِيكَيْنِ: two partners in a shared financial or business relationship
key_terms.نَصِيبٌ: a share, portion, or personal stake in the matter

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of one business partner for another accepted in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the testimony of business partners. A partner’s testimony for the other is accepted in general, but not in a matter where the testifying partner has a personal share or direct interest.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3293 - And Fadalah narrated from Aban, who said:

Abu Abdullah (as), was asked about two partners, one of whom testified for the other.
Imam (as) said: "His testimony is valid except in something where he has a share."
